title: Quarterly lane optimizer & decision canvas for hosted endpoint fleet
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a decision-driven quarterly plan that maps endpoint tiers, commitment lanes, and model-catalog governance to measurable OKRs. Deliver an operational canvas (playable artifact) for quarterly planning meetings and an enforceable checklist for release windows.
goals: Define 3 commitment lanes (Baseline, Surge, Canary) with clear capacity/backstop policies
Link each lane to OKRs and SLO impact metrics (p95 latency, unit cost delta, model quality score)
Produce a decision canvas used by PM/Eng/Capacity teams during sprint planning
Ship a lightweight governance checklist for model catalog rotations and retirements
scope: Hosted API endpoints (non-dedicated) only — Dedicated and Private will be referenced but out of scope
Model catalog entries that are eligible for automated rotation or fallbacks
Stakeholder alignment artifact and playbook (not automation code)
One-quarter pilot with two customer cohorts (internal apps + small external PLG customers)
milestones: 2026-01-26: First draft decision canvas + OKR mapping
2026-03-10: Publish playbook to Confluence and circulate to GTM
acceptance_criteria: Decision canvas with lanes and policy knobs published to Confluence
OKR-to-metric mapping doc completed and validated by Analytics
Two pilot endpoints run under the new lanes with telemetry captured
Governance checklist signed off by Security and Legal (if model retirements involve IP)
risks: Capacity estimates rely on coarse telemetry — may under/over provision
Stakeholder alignment might slip if GTM objections surface late
Model quality regressions not caught by current evals could break customer experience
Ambiguity about which catalog entries qualify for automatic rotation
dependencies: ENG-18204 (Autoscaler policy surface for surge lanes)
ENG-19021 (Telemetry: add lane tags to traces)
